Name: 0_forced_banks_im_account
Representative_Docs:
['Worst forced app update in history?. Being overseas without my Australian mobile, I was forced to upgrade the app after receiving warnings the current app would stop working and I would lose access to internet banking. But to update, I needed to get an Australian SIM to receive the SMS one-time PIN which is required by the new app to finish the update. It wasn’t easy but I did it, and after upgrading I was surprised that the new interface - design and functionality - seemed like something a child had done! Essential functions either didn’t work or exist such as the basic task of being able to contact ING via secure message - offered by every bank I have used. Months later, things still don’t work in the new app. Bugs I won’t bother going into. Almost every review of this app is 1 star and the bugs are endless. Customer service were totally uninformed about the app upgrade when I called them and several times I received incorrect information about whether the old app would stop working on the date mentioned in the warning. Seems like ING is cutting corners everywhere - from IT to customer service - I can’t imagine anyone investing in a company/bank that operates like this. Update: I still receive messages saying “update before the app stops working” out of nowhere, which is concerning being overseas without phone network and potentially needing a new mobile to receive a one time PIN again. So many people have switched banks because of this nightmare update.', 'Two minutes in and I hate it. Rant incoming!
I really hope ING is taking the terrible star ratings of this new app seriously. I’ve used it for about TWO MINUTES and I’ve already come across multiple issues and I’m sure I’ll find more as I’m forced to use it.

Firstly, when transferring money, the app is now hell-bent on you getting the recipient’s account name precise. This was never an issue for me in the old app. If I had the correct BSB and account number, I could make the transfer without fighting with the app over exactly how someone’s account name is formatted.

Secondly, what on earth happened to sharing bank details? Previously, when I copied my account details, ING gave me a simple, nicely formatted message:

“My ING account details are:
BSB: ******
ACC: *********”

Now when I copy my details, I get my BSB and account number MASHED TOGETHER into one giant line of numbers with no labels or formatting whatsoever. Who thought that was an improvement? The entire purpose of copying bank details is to make them easy to share accurately.

Did you actually test this app  before launching it and forcing your existing customers to switch?

There’s an old saying: WHY FIX WHAT AIN’T BROKE?

The old ING app was simple, intuitive and functional. That simplicity was part of what made ING good. This new app feels like someone redesigned things for the sake of redesigning them without a thought about user experience. 

And please, for the love of God, stop replacing perfectly functional features with things that feel like they were designed by AI without anyone checking whether the end result makes any sense.

This is dumb, sloppy work. You’re going to lose loyal customers who were loyal precisely because ING felt smarter and simpler than the alternatives.

Do better, ING. Fix it.', 'Very disappointed. I was forced to switch to the new ING app, and it’s one of the most frustrating banking app updates I’ve experienced. The previous app was simple, intuitive, and made managing my finances quick and easy. This redesign has done the exact opposite.

Previously, I had my accounts organised exactly how I wanted them, making it easy to distinguish between my everyday accounts, long-term savings, and credit card. The new app has removed that clarity, and it’s now difficult to quickly identify which account is which.

The biggest issue is the loss of easy access to my credit card. I used to be able to check my balance and transactions at a glance throughout the day, but that functionality now appears to be buried or missing altogether.

Another major frustration is that my partner and I could previously use the same phone and simply switch between our individual ING accounts. That feature has been removed, making the app far less practical for our household.

This update feels like a redesign for the sake of redesign, rather than an improvement to the user experience. Core functionality has been made more complicated, navigation is less intuitive, and tasks that were once quick now take far more effort.

I’ve banked with ING for years because of its excellent digital experience, but this update has seriously undermined that. Unless these issues are addressed, I’ll be looking at moving my banking elsewhere. I genuinely hope ING listens to the overwhelming customer feedback and prioritises usability over aesthetics.']
